title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
description: Roman pasta bound with egg yolk and pecorino — never cream.
steps: Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil and drop in the spaghetti.
While it cooks, dice the bacon and render it slowly in a dry frying pan until the fat runs and the edges crisp.
Beat the egg yolks with the grated pecorino and a heavy grind of black pepper until it forms a thick paste.
Drain the pasta, reserving a mugful of the cooking water, and tip it into the pan with the bacon off the heat.
Stir the yolk mixture through immediately, loosening with splashes of pasta water until the sauce coats each strand.
Serve at once with more pecorino and pepper — it stiffens as it cools.

title: Spicy Arrabiata Penne
description: Angry red sauce: garlic, chilli and tomatoes, done in the time the pasta boils.
steps: Put the penne on to boil in heavily salted water.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan and soften the sliced garlic gently — let it turn pale gold, not brown.
Add the chilli flakes and Italian seasoning and let them sizzle for a few seconds to release their oils.
Tip in the chopped tomatoes, season, and simmer hard until the sauce darkens and pulls away from the pan.
Toss the drained penne through the sauce, tear in the basil, and finish with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.

title: Massaman Beef curry
description: Slow-braised Thai curry with peanuts, potato and warm whole spices.

ingredients.name: Brown sugar, palm or soft light
chilli, red deseeded and finely sliced, to serve

steps: Roast the peanuts on a tray in a hot oven until golden, then cool and chop them roughly. Drop the oven to 180C.
Heat a few spoonfuls of the coconut cream in a casserole and fry the curry paste until it smells fragrant.
Stir in the beef and turn it until every piece is coated and sealed.
Pour in the remaining coconut cream with half a can of water, then add the potatoes, onion wedges, lime leaves and cinnamon stick.
Cover and braise in the oven until the beef shreds under a fork and the potatoes are soft.
Season with tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce, balancing until it tastes sour, sweet and salty at once.
Scatter over the peanuts and sliced red chilli and serve with jasmine rice.

title: Tom yum soup with prawns
description: Hot-and-sour prawn broth sharpened with lemongrass, galangal and lime.
steps: Bruise the lemongrass stalks and slice the galangal, then simmer both in the stock with the lime leaves to build the base.
Add the onion and tomato wedges and cook until they just soften.
Stir in the chilli jam and coconut milk and bring back to a gentle simmer.
Drop in the prawns and oyster mushrooms and poach until the prawns turn opaque.
Take the pan off the heat before seasoning with fish sauce and lime juice — boiling dulls both.
Taste and adjust until it is aggressively sour and salty, then finish with coriander.

title: Beef Rendang
description: Dry Malaysian curry cooked down until the coconut caramelises onto the meat.
steps: Blend the shallots into a paste and fry them in the oil with the cinnamon, cloves, star anise and cardamom until aromatic.
Add the beef and turn it in the spice paste until sealed on all sides.
Pour in the coconut cream and water, then add the tamarind paste, lime and sugar.
Simmer uncovered, stirring often, and let the liquid reduce right down.
Keep going past the point it looks done — the sauce should darken, split and cling to the meat.
Rest for at least ten minutes before serving; overnight is better still.

title: Beef pho
description: Vietnamese noodle soup with a charred-aromatic broth and raw sliced steak.
steps: Char the halved onion and ginger directly over a flame or under a hot grill until blackened in patches.
Toast the cinnamon, star anise, coriander seeds and cloves in a dry pan until they smell fragrant.
Add the charred aromatics and toasted spices to the beef stock and steep at the barest simmer.
Strain the broth, then season with fish sauce, soy sauce and palm sugar.
Soak the rice noodles until pliable and divide them between four deep bowls.
Lay the thinly sliced raw sirloin over the noodles and ladle the boiling broth straight on top.
Serve with spring onions, herbs, chilli and lime for everyone to add themselves.

title: Vegan banh mi
description: Crisp baguette, quick pickles and marinated tempeh — the meat-free banh mi.
steps: Shred the raw vegetables finely and toss them with the vinegar and sugar. Leave them to pickle while you do everything else.
Slice the tempeh and fry it until deeply golden on both sides.
Split the baguette lengthways without cutting all the way through, and pull out a little of the soft crumb.
Spread the hummus thickly along the base.
Layer in the tempeh, drained pickles and a generous amount of coriander and mint.
Add hot sauce to taste and press the sandwich closed firmly before cutting.

title: Sweet and Sour Chicken
description: Crisp velveted chicken in a pineapple and ketchup glaze.
steps: Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and toss them with the egg white, salt and cornstarch. Rest for fifteen minutes.
Whisk the pineapple juice, vinegar, ketchup and brown sugar together and set the sauce aside.
Get a wok very hot, add the oil, and fry the chicken in batches until golden and cooked through.
Lift the chicken out, then stir-fry the peppers and ginger briefly so they keep some bite.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and add the pineapple chunks.
Bubble until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.

title: Kung Po Prawns
description: Fiery Sichuan-style prawns with peanuts and water chestnuts.
steps: Toss the prawns with the soy sauce, tomato puree, corn flour and caster sugar and leave them to marinate.
Prepare everything else first — sliced chillies, chopped garlic, drained water chestnuts — and line it up by the hob.
Heat the sunflower oil in a wok until it shimmers, then fry the garlic and chillies for a few seconds only.
Add the prawns and stir-fry hard until they curl and turn pink.
Throw in the water chestnuts, peanuts and brown sugar and toss everything together for a final minute.

title: Ma Po Tofu
description: Silken tofu in a numbing Sichuan sauce with minced beef.
steps: Cut the tofu into cubes and slide them into lightly salted warm water to firm up while you cook.
Toast the Sichuan pepper in a dry wok, then grind it coarsely and set it aside.
Brown the minced beef in the olive oil until it is properly crisp rather than just grey.
Add the doubanjiang, fermented black beans, garlic and ginger and fry until the oil turns red.
Pour in the water and soy sauce, then drain the tofu and slide it in, nudging rather than stirring.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry, then finish with sesame oil, the ground Sichuan pepper and spring onions.

title: Katsu Chicken curry
description: Panko-crumbed chicken with a mellow, lightly sweet Japanese curry sauce.
steps: Soften the onions, garlic and carrot in the sunflower oil over a low heat until sweet.
Stir in the flour, curry powder and garam masala and cook out the raw taste.
Add the stock gradually, then the honey, soy sauce and bay leaf, and simmer until thickened.
Blend the sauce and pass it through a sieve — this is what makes it glossy rather than grainy.
Dredge the pounded chicken breasts in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Shallow-fry until deep golden and cooked through, then drain on kitchen paper.
Slice the katsu thickly and serve over rice with the sauce poured alongside.

title: Tonkatsu pork
description: Panko-crusted pork chops with a tangy brown tonkatsu sauce.
steps: Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce and sugar together until the sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Bat the pork chops out to an even thickness and season them well on both sides.
Set up three bowls — flour, beaten egg, breadcrumbs — and coat each chop in that order.
Heat the oil to the point where a crumb sizzles immediately, then fry the chops until deep golden.
Rest on a rack rather than paper so the underside stays crisp.
Slice across into strips and serve with the sauce.

title: Japanese Katsudon
description: Pork cutlet simmered with onion and egg, served over rice.
steps: Cook the sushi rice and keep it warm and covered.
Slice the onion thinly and soften it in the oil in a small frying pan.
Add the stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar and bring to a simmer.
Lay the chopped pork in the pan and let it warm through in the broth.
Pour the beaten eggs over the top and cover — take it off while they are still soft and barely set.
Slide the whole thing onto the rice and scatter with chives.

title: Sushi
description: Seasoned sushi rice rolled with cucumber and a spiced mayonnaise.
steps: Rinse the sushi rice in several changes of cold water until it runs clear.
Cook the rice, then spread it out in a wide dish and fold the rice wine and sugar through with a cutting motion while it cools.
Stir the mayonnaise with the remaining rice wine and soy sauce to make the dressing.
Cut the cucumber into long batons, discarding the watery seed core.
Spread rice thinly over the nori, leaving a clear border along the far edge, and lay the cucumber across the near third.
Roll tightly away from you using the mat, sealing the border with a dab of water.
Slice with a wet blade, wiping between cuts, and serve with the spiced mayonnaise.

title: Lamb Tagine
description: Moroccan braise of lamb, apricots and squash with saffron and cinnamon.
steps: Brown the diced lamb hard in the olive oil, in batches, and lift it out.
Soften the onion and carrots in the same pan, scraping up everything stuck to the base.
Add the garlic, cumin, ginger, saffron and cinnamon and fry until the kitchen smells of them.
Return the lamb with the stock cube, honey and enough water to almost cover.
Cover and cook at a bare simmer until the lamb is yielding.
Add the apricots and butternut squash and cook until the squash is tender but still holds its shape.
Rest, then serve over steamed couscous with plenty of chopped parsley.

title: Chicken Couscous
description: One-pan harissa chicken with chickpeas, apricots and fluffy couscous.
steps: Soften the chopped onion in the olive oil until translucent.
Add the diced chicken breast and brown it lightly on all sides.
Stir in the harissa and ginger and coat everything well.
Add the chickpeas and chopped apricots with a splash of the stock and simmer until the chicken is cooked through.
Tip in the couscous, pour over the remaining hot stock, cover and take off the heat.
Fork the grains through to separate them and finish with torn coriander.

title: Lamb and Lemon Souvlaki
description: Charred lamb skewers marinated in garlic, lemon and dill.
steps: Crush the garlic to a paste with the sea salt using the flat of a knife.
Whisk it into the olive oil with the lemon zest and juice and the chopped dill.
Cube the lamb leg, turn it through the marinade, and refrigerate.
Thread onto skewers, leaving a little space between pieces so the heat gets around them.
Grill over a high heat, turning, until charred outside and pink within.
Rest briefly and serve stuffed into warm pita.

title: Chicken Quinoa Greek Salad
description: Warm quinoa with chilli-garlic chicken, feta, olives and mint.
steps: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly — the coating on the outside is bitter — then cook it and let it steam dry.
Melt the butter with the olive oil and fry the chopped chilli and garlic briefly.
Add the sliced chicken breast and cook until golden and firm.
Fold the warm quinoa through the pan so it takes up the buttery juices.
Add the olives, red onion and lemon juice and toss.
Crumble the feta over at the last moment and finish with torn mint.

title: Turkish lahmacun
description: Paper-thin Turkish flatbread under a spiced minced lamb topping.
steps: Mix the flour and yeast with warm water and salt, then knead until smooth and elastic.
Leave the dough covered somewhere warm until doubled.
Blitz the tomatoes, green chillies, spring onions, parsley and olive oil to a coarse paste.
Work the paste into the ground beef with the chilli flakes, cumin and allspice.
Heat the oven as high as it will go with a baking stone or heavy tray inside.
Roll each dough ball out paper-thin on a cornfloured surface and spread the topping right to the edge.
Bake until the edges blister and the meat is just cooked.
Serve with lemon wedges and sliced red onion to roll up inside.

title: Turkish lamb pilau
description: Spiced rice baked with lamb, apricots and toasted pine nuts.
steps: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden and tip them straight out — they carry on cooking in a hot pan.
Brown the diced lamb in the olive oil and set it aside.
Soften the chopped onion with the cinnamon sticks in the same pan.
Stir the rinsed basmati through the fat until every grain is coated and glossy.
Return the lamb, add the apricots and hot stock, cover tightly and cook without stirring.
Rest off the heat, still covered, then fork through with the pine nuts and mint.

title: Kumpir
description: Turkish street-food baked potato whipped with butter and cheese.
steps: Prick the potatoes all over, rub them with salt, and bake until the skins are crisp and they give under pressure.
Split each one lengthways without cutting through the base.
Work the butter and grated cheese into the hot flesh with a fork, right there in the skin, until smooth and fluffy.
Pile on the chopped onion and red pepper.
Finish with a pinch of red chilli flakes.

title: Gambas al ajillo
description: Prawns sizzled in garlic chilli oil — five ingredients, six minutes.
steps: Slice the garlic thinly and halve the dried cayenne peppers.
Heat the olive oil in a small earthenware or heavy pan until it shimmers.
Add the garlic and chilli and let them sizzle for a few seconds only.
Slide in the prawns in a single layer and cook until they curl and turn opaque.
Scatter with parsley and take it to the table still spitting, with bread.

title: Ham croquetas
description: Molten jamón béchamel in a crisp fried shell.
steps: Sweat the finely chopped leek in the olive oil until completely soft but uncoloured.
Add the chopped jamón and warm it through.
Stir in the flour and cook it out properly — a raw roux ruins the whole batch.
Add the milk and stock a little at a time, beating hard, until you have a very thick, smooth paste.
Season with grated nutmeg, spread into a shallow tray, cover and chill until firm.
Shape into barrels, then roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry in batches until deep gold, and drain on a rack.

title: Salt cod tortilla
description: Spanish potato omelette enriched with flakes of salt cod.
steps: Soak the salt cod in several changes of cold water, then drain and flake it, discarding any skin and bone.
Slice the potatoes thinly and poach them gently in the olive oil with the onion until tender but not browned.
Add the chopped garlic for the last minute, then drain, reserving the oil.
Beat the eggs with the parsley, then fold through the warm potatoes and flaked cod. Rest the mixture.
Return a little oil to the pan and pour the mixture in, drawing the edges inward as it sets.
Invert onto a plate and slide it back in to finish the other side, keeping the centre soft.
Rest for ten minutes before cutting — it firms as it sits.

title: Padron peppers
description: Blistered Galician peppers with sea salt. Roughly one in ten bites back.
steps: Wash the peppers and dry them completely — any water left on them will steam instead of blister.
Get a heavy frying pan properly smoking, then add the olive oil.
Throw the peppers in and leave them alone until the skins blacken in patches.
Toss and repeat until they are blistered all over and starting to slump.
Tip into a bowl and shower with flaky sea salt. Eat immediately with your fingers.

title: Chicken Enchilada Casserole
description: Layered tortillas, shredded chicken and Monterey Jack, baked until bubbling.
steps: Poach the chicken breasts until cooked through, then shred them with two forks.
Heat the oven to 190C and spoon a thin layer of enchilada sauce over the base of a baking dish.
Lay down tortillas, then chicken, then sauce, then cheese — and repeat until everything is used.
Finish with a heavy layer of Monterey Jack on top.
Bake until the cheese is molten and blistered at the edges.
Rest for ten minutes before cutting or it will slide apart.

title: Cajun spiced fish tacos
description: Blackened white fish in soft tortillas with avocado and lime crema.
steps: Mix the cajun seasoning with the cayenne and rub it over the fish fillets on both sides.
Stir the garlic and a squeeze of lemon through the sour cream to make a quick crema.
Get a heavy pan very hot with the vegetable oil.
Sear the fish without moving it until a dark crust forms, then turn once.
Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry pan until flexible.
Flake the fish into the tortillas and top with lettuce, spring onion, avocado, salsa and crema.

title: Dal fry
description: Soft toor dal finished with a sizzling ghee tempering.
steps: Rinse the toor dal until the water runs clear, then simmer it with the water, salt and turmeric until completely soft.
Whisk the cooked dal briefly to break it down to a loose, creamy consistency.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and add the cumin and mustard seeds — wait for them to pop.
Add the bay leaves, green chilli and shredded ginger and fry until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and red pepper and cook until the fat separates out.
Pour the tempering into the dal, add the garam masala, and simmer briefly to bring it together.
Finish with chopped cilantro and a pinch of sugar to balance.

title: Baingan Bharta
description: Smoke-roasted aubergine mashed with tomato, garlic and green chilli.
steps: Rub the aubergine with a little oil and char it directly over a gas flame, turning, until the skin is blackened all over and it collapses.
Leave it to cool in a covered bowl — the trapped steam loosens the skin.
Peel away the burnt skin and mash the flesh coarsely with a fork.
Fry the garlic and green chilli in the remaining oil until golden.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then the tomatoes and red chilli powder.
Stir the mashed aubergine in and cook it down until the oil separates.
Season and finish with chopped coriander leaves.

title: Matar Paneer
description: Paneer and peas in a spiced tomato gravy.
steps: Cube the paneer and fry it in the sunflower oil until pale gold on each side, then lift it out.
Add the cumin to the same pan and let it crackle.
Grate in the ginger and green chilli, then add the chopped tomatoes with the turmeric and ground coriander.
Cook the gravy down hard until it darkens and the oil pools at the edges.
Add the peas and a splash of water and simmer until tender.
Return the paneer, add the garam masala, and warm through without boiling.
Scatter with coriander and serve with naan.

title: Full English Breakfast
description: The full plate: sausage, bacon, black pudding, eggs, beans and fried bread.
steps: Start the sausages in a cold pan over a medium heat and turn them regularly — they need the longest.
Heat the oven low and use it to hold everything as it finishes.
Add the bacon to the pan and cook to your preference, then move it to the oven.
Halve the tomatoes and cook them cut-side down with the mushrooms and sliced black pudding.
Warm the baked beans through in a small pan.
Fry the bread in the rendered bacon fat until crisp and golden on both sides.
Fry the eggs last, basting with hot fat, and plate everything immediately.

title: Smoked Haddock Kedgeree
description: Anglo-Indian breakfast rice with smoked haddock and soft-boiled eggs.
steps: Poach the smoked haddock gently in the stock until it flakes, then lift it out and reserve the liquid.
Soft-boil the eggs, cool them under running water and peel.
Melt the butter and soften the chopped onion with the cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, bay and turmeric.
Stir the basmati through the spiced butter until the grains are coated.
Pour in the reserved poaching stock, cover, and cook without stirring until the liquid is absorbed.
Flake the haddock through the rice, keeping the pieces large.
Quarter the eggs over the top and finish with parsley and lemon.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: Date-free treacle sponge drowned in hot muscovado toffee sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and butter a deep baking dish.
Cream the butter and muscovado sugar until light, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and bicarbonate, then the black treacle and milk — the batter will be very loose.
Pour into the dish and bake until risen and springy in the centre.
For the sauce, melt the butter, muscovado sugar and treacle together, then stir in the cream and vanilla.
Simmer until it thickens and darkens slightly.
Prick the hot sponge all over and pour a third of the sauce in, serving the rest at the table with cream.

title: Eton Mess
description: Crushed meringue, strawberries and whipped cream. Assembled, not cooked.
steps: Hull the strawberries. Set half aside and roughly crush the rest with the ginger cordial.
Leave the crushed fruit to macerate and release its juice.
Whip the double cream to soft peaks — stop well before it stiffens.
Break the meringue nests into uneven pieces, keeping some large.
Fold the cream, meringue, chopped strawberries and crushed fruit together in three or four strokes only.
Spoon into glasses and top with a sprig of mint. Serve straight away.

title: Bakewell tart
description: Shortcrust shell, raspberry jam and almond frangipane under flaked almonds.
steps: Rub the chilled butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs, then bring it together with the cold water.
Wrap and chill the pastry before rolling — warm pastry shrinks in the tin.
Line the tart tin, prick the base, and blind-bake with beans until pale gold and dry.
Beat the butter and caster sugar together, then work in the ground almonds, beaten egg and almond extract.
Spread the raspberry jam over the cooled base and level the frangipane over it.
Scatter with flaked almonds and bake until risen, firm and golden.
Cool in the tin — it is too fragile to move while hot.

title: Vegan Chocolate Cake
description: One-bowl chocolate cake with flax eggs and almond milk.
steps: Make the flax eggs by stirring ground flaxseed into water and leaving them to thicken to a gel.
Heat the oven to 180C and line a round cake tin.
Whisk the self-raising flour, coco sugar, raw cacao and baking powder together in one bowl.
Stir in the flax eggs, almond milk and vanilla until just combined — do not beat it.
Pour in the boiling water last and mix to a very thin batter.
Bake until a skewer comes out with a few damp crumbs rather than clean.
Cool in the tin for ten minutes before turning out.
